items.context: The GET /api/v1/scenarios endpoint needs to return scenario metadata (name, description). The scenarios directory contains service.json files in some scenarios but the format varies. We need to decide how to source display metadata.

options.label: Read service.json from each scenario directory
options.rationale: Most accurate — uses the scenario's own declared metadata. Already used by other parts of Vrooli. Handles missing files gracefully by falling back to directory name.

options.label: Use directory names only (no metadata files)
options.rationale: Simplest implementation — just list directories. No display name or description available. Fast but low-information.

options.label: Call vrooli CLI to list scenarios
options.rationale: Consistent with how swarm-manager lists scenarios. Adds a subprocess dependency but leverages existing tooling. May be slower.

items.context: The ScenarioPicker needs to integrate into both BrandFormPage (inline selection) and BrandDetailPage (change/assign action). We need to decide the component pattern.

options.label: Inline dropdown/combobox on the form, dialog for detail page
options.rationale: Most natural UX — dropdown fits inline in creation form, dialog is appropriate for the 'change scenario' action on detail page. Two render modes from one component.

options.label: Always a modal dialog
options.rationale: Consistent pattern everywhere. Slightly heavier for the creation form where an inline picker would feel lighter.

options.label: Dedicated page with navigation
options.rationale: Full page for scenario selection. Most room for rich scenario cards but interrupts the form flow.

items.topic: Assignment creation timing on brand create
items.context: When a user creates a brand with a scenario selected, we need to create the assignment. This could be two sequential API calls from the UI or a server-side orchestration.

options.label: Two sequential client-side calls (create brand, then create assignment)
options.rationale: Simple, transparent, uses existing endpoints. If assignment fails, brand still exists and user can retry from detail page. No new API contract needed.

options.label: New combined endpoint: POST /api/v1/brands with optional scenario_name field
options.rationale: Atomic — either both succeed or neither does. Requires API contract change and transaction handling. More complex but prevents orphan state.

items.context: The assignments table has UNIQUE(scenario_name), so each scenario can only have one brand. When displaying the picker, scenarios already assigned to another brand could be shown differently.

options.label: Show all scenarios, mark assigned ones with a badge showing brand name
options.rationale: Full visibility — user sees everything and understands what's taken. Selecting an assigned scenario would reassign it (with confirmation). Most flexible.

options.label: Hide already-assigned scenarios entirely
options.rationale: Cleanest picker — only available options shown. But user can't discover or reassign from this flow.

options.label: Show assigned scenarios as disabled/grayed out
options.rationale: User sees what exists but can't accidentally reassign. Must go to the other brand's detail page to unassign first.

items.text: The existing ApplyPreview component in the UI uses a manual text input for scenario name. The new ScenarioPicker will replace this pattern with a structured selection. ApplyPreview may be refactored to use ScenarioPicker internally, or kept as-is if it serves a different use case (e.g., applying to scenarios not yet in the directory).

plan_updates: Created initial plan scaffold with all 13 mandatory sections. Defined 4-phase implementation strategy (API endpoint, picker component, form integration, detail page integration). Documented current technical context from codebase exploration.
